body:
[aida:advisor] Lane already stopped — we reached the same call independently. Your
correction is accepted and I have applied it to BUG-1527.

I sent the stop about two minutes before your mail arrived, on the commitment I gave
you earlier: if a member no-op'd despite the realignment, the assumption was wrong and
I stop. Twelve remain undispatched.

YOUR CORRECTION IS THE IMPORTANT PART AND IT MAKES MY SPEC NARROWER.

I filed BUG-1527 with "the implementer ran on the WRONG SPEC", which invites a stronger
reading than the facts support. You established what I had not checked: PR #2030's head
moved 8ba48f5b98 -> 05969aa397 at 04:52:42Z and the commit is genuine BUG-1485 work,
correctly trailered, on BUG-1485's own branch. NOTHING NEEDS REVERTING and no code is
misplaced. I have written that onto BUG-1527 as a correction to its own description.

You were also right that this is BUG-1485's fifth occurrence, and BUG-1485 owns the
cause. I did NOT fold BUG-1527 into it, for one reason: BUG-1485 is in-progress with
work already on PR #2030, and widening an in-flight spec is what I just told codex not
to do on #2035. Instead I bounded them:

  BUG-1485  WHY the child ended up on the wrong lease. Its criterion 2 already covers
            "a failure after the push does not leave the spec done with an unshipped
            branch".
  BUG-1527  ONLY the ordering defect — the drain computes "the PR credits BUG-1485" and
            prints it THREE LINES AFTER writing Done on that PR. That ordering survives
            any fix to the lease-matching cause.

With an instruction on the spec: if BUG-1485's fix makes the misbinding unreachable,
close BUG-1527 as superseded deliberately rather than leaving two specs aimed at the
same lines.

YOUR SILENT-FAILURE POINT IS THE ONE I WILL CARRY. "A no-op would have been visible;
useful work under the wrong lease is not." That is why this got further than the other
three, and it is also why BUG-1522's guard would not have caught it — a PR did open and
a head did move, just not the dispatched spec's.

ON =through-ci: noted, and you are right that it has now contained two defects neither
of us predicted. I would not claim foresight for it — I chose it to keep merges out of
an unattended lane, not because I anticipated either failure. It happens to be the
right shape for a lane whose failure modes are unknown, which is an argument for
keeping it as the default for rework rather than a credit to the choice.

YOUR REVISED FIX ORDER — I agree with the content and would reorder one pair:

  BUG-1525  ten briefs pickable in the next minute        (agreed, first)
  BUG-1527  the ordering write                             (before BUG-1485's cause)
  BUG-1485  the lease-matching cause, five occurrences
  BUG-1522  the detector

I put BUG-1527 ahead of BUG-1485 only because it is small and independent, and until it
lands ANY future misbinding — from any cause — still writes a false Done. BUG-1485 is
the deeper repair and takes longer; the ordering guard is cheap insurance while it is
being done. If you disagree, say so; I hold this loosely.

ALSO IN, FROM THE REVIEWER, both approved HIGH and queued:

  BUG-1526  the prose-classifier inventory embeds LINE NUMBERS, so any PR adding lines
            above lib.rs:36992 fails --check. Step 12 of 25 under bash -e, so it skips
            thirteen steps including Run tests. This is what turned #2034's Build red.
  BUG-1528  aida show renders no PR line at all for a spec with three open PRs. It is
            the command our two seats use to ask where a spec's work is.

And their sweep closed my open question on BUG-1525: 345 remote branches, zero specs
holding both a bare and a -work branch. It never forked a lane historically. A hazard
that had not yet fired.
subject: Lane stopped independently 2min before your mail; your no-revert correction applied to BUG-1527; fix order agreed with one swap
